# Text tools reference

This page lists the names exported by `@sefaria/text-transform` and the HTML that `normalizeText` produces. `normalizeText` makes Sefaria's HTML safe to display. Run it before `applyVocalizationToHtml`, which doesn't sanitize. `createTextPreview` accepts raw HTML and normalizes it itself.

## Which release this describes

This page documents the code on the `main` branch. The source stamp is not an npm release or a development snapshot. <ReleaseStamp />

Install an exact npm version or use a version-pinned npm CDN module. The npm `alpha` tag moves between reviewed prereleases. It is not a main-build snapshot. Older pinned releases keep their own behavior and can lack APIs added since. [Install and status](/help/install-and-status.md) lists package commands and jsDelivr/UNPKG files.

## Functions and types

Import all of these from the package root.

### Functions

#### applyVocalization()

```ts
function applyVocalization(text, mode, options?): string;
```

Applies a vocalization preset to plain text without Unicode normalization.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                          |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `text`    | `string`                                      |
| `mode`    | [`VocalizationMode`](#vocalizationmode)       |
| `options` | [`VocalizationOptions`](#vocalizationoptions) |

##### Returns

`string`

##### Throws

When a runtime mode or PASEQ value is unsupported.

#### applyVocalizationToHtml()

```ts
function applyVocalizationToHtml(html, mode, options?): string;
```

Applies vocalization only to text nodes in an already-sanitized HTML fragment.

Run [normalizeText](#normalizetext) first. Markup and attribute values are preserved. This operation is not a sanitizer.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                          |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `html`    | `string`                                      |
| `mode`    | [`VocalizationMode`](#vocalizationmode)       |
| `options` | [`VocalizationOptions`](#vocalizationoptions) |

##### Returns

`string`

##### Throws

When a runtime mode or PASEQ value is unsupported.

#### createTextPreview()

```ts
function createTextPreview(input, maximumGraphemes?): TextPreview;
```

Accepts raw HTML, normalizes it, and bounds rendered graphemes across inline node boundaries. Footnotes, annotations, and link interaction are omitted from this compact view.

##### Parameters

| Parameter          | Type     | Default value |
| ------------------ | -------- | ------------- |
| `input`            | `string` | —             |
| `maximumGraphemes` | `number` | `3500`        |

##### Returns

[`TextPreview`](#textpreview)

---

#### normalizeText()

```ts
function normalizeText(html, options?): NormalizedText;
```

Converts untrusted Sefaria text markup into safe, directly renderable HTML.

The operation parses once, removes unsupported attributes, emits no URLs, and extracts footnotes into result-local records. Options can narrow but never widen the fixed output grammar.

##### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                            |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `html`    | `string`                                        |
| `options` | [`NormalizeTextOptions`](#normalizetextoptions) |

##### Returns

[`NormalizedText`](#normalizedtext)

##### Remarks

Output keeps only these ordinary inline tags without attributes: `b`, `strong`, `i`, `em`, `u`, `small`, `sup`, and `sub`. It keeps `br`, maps `big` to `<span style="font-size: larger;">`, converts `img` to its `alt` text, unwraps block elements with separators, and removes active content. Incoming style attributes are dropped. The fixed `font-size: larger;` style emitted for `big` is the only output style. The only ordinary attribute is `dir`, and only on `i` or generated `span` elements when the value is `ltr`, `rtl`, or `auto`.

Recognized structural attributes are `data-sefaria-note`, `data-sefaria-end-footnote`, `data-sefaria-commentary-marker`, `data-sefaria-commentator`, `data-sefaria-label`, `data-sefaria-order`, `data-sefaria-overlay`, `data-sefaria-value`, `data-sefaria-ref`, `data-sefaria-ven`, `data-sefaria-vhe`, `data-sefaria-slug`, and `data-sefaria-mam`. Footnote placeholders use `data-sefaria-note` values that match note keys in [NormalizedText.notes](#property-notes).

##### Example

```ts
normalizeText(
  'See <a data-ref="Micah 6:8" href="/Micah.6.8">Micah</a><script>x()</script>',
).bodyHtml;
// 'See <span data-sefaria-ref="Micah 6:8">Micah</span>'
```

##### Throws

When commentary reference input is invalid.

##### Throws

When projected output exceeds `max(65_536, html.length * 8)` UTF-16 code units.

#### NormalizeTextOptions

Feature-narrowing inputs for [normalizeText](#normalizetext).

##### Properties

| Property | Modifier | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="property-allowfootnotes"></a> `allowFootnotes?` | `readonly` | `boolean` | Retain recognized footnotes. Defaults to `true`. When enabled, footnote markers keep `data-sefaria-note` placeholders whose values are result-local note keys. End-of-text markers also keep `data-sefaria-end-footnote` when [allowInlineAnnotations](#property-allowinlineannotations) is enabled. |
| <a id="property-allowinlineannotations"></a> `allowInlineAnnotations?` | `readonly` | `boolean` | Retain commentary, overlay, and standalone annotation metadata. Defaults to `true`. When enabled, end-of-text footnote markers keep `data-sefaria-end-footnote` when `allowFootnotes` is also enabled, commentary markers keep `data-sefaria-commentary-marker`, commentary anchors keep `data-sefaria-commentator`, `data-sefaria-label`, and `data-sefaria-order`; matching commentary references can add `data-sefaria-ref`. Overlay anchors keep `data-sefaria-overlay` plus `data-sefaria-value`. When disabled, those attributes and their empty anchor elements are dropped. |
| <a id="property-allownamedentities"></a> `allowNamedEntities?` | `readonly` | `boolean` | Retain named-entity identity as `data-sefaria-slug`. Defaults to `true`. When disabled, named-entity links are unwrapped and only their text remains. |
| <a id="property-allowreflinks"></a> `allowRefLinks?` | `readonly` | `boolean` | Retain explicit Sefaria reference identity. Defaults to `true`. When enabled, reference links keep `data-sefaria-ref` and optional `data-sefaria-ven`, `data-sefaria-vhe`, and approved `dir`. When disabled, reference links are unwrapped and those attributes are dropped. |
| <a id="property-commentaryreferences"></a> `commentaryReferences?` | `readonly` | readonly [`CommentaryReference`](#commentaryreference)[] | Optional exact commentary targets prepared from source-scoped link evidence. Matching entries add `data-sefaria-ref` to commentary anchors that are also retained by [allowInlineAnnotations](#property-allowinlineannotations). The value is dropped when there is no exact, unique match. |

<a id="normalized-html-output"></a>

## Normalized HTML output

`normalizeText` returns `bodyHtml` and footnote HTML with no links, no event handlers and no scripts. It emits only the attributes listed in this section, plus approved `dir` values and the fixed `style` value generated for `<big>`. Addresses can still appear as ordinary text or inside an attribute value, such as a reference. This section is generated from `normalize.ts`, and each example below is the function's real output.

### Elements

- These formatting elements are kept, with no attributes except `dir` on `<i>`: `<b>`, `<strong>`, `<i>`, `<em>`, `<u>`, `<small>`, `<sup>`, `<sub>`.
- `<br>` is kept with no attributes.
- `<big>` becomes `<span style="font-size: larger;">`. This is the only `style` attribute in the output. Incoming styles are removed.
- `<img>` is replaced by its `alt` text.
- Toolkit-specific markup is output as `<span>` elements with the attributes below.
- Block elements, such as `<blockquote>`, are unwrapped with a separator kept between their contents.
- Scripts, styles and similar active content are removed. Other elements are unwrapped, keeping their text.
- `dir` is kept only when its value is `ltr`, `rtl` or `auto`.

### Attributes

The last column names the `NormalizeTextOptions` setting that controls the markup. The four `allow…` settings default to `true`. `commentaryReferences` defaults to none, so a commentary anchor gets `data-sefaria-ref` only when you supply a matching reference. Masorah markings are kept when a `<span>` has exactly one recognized Masorah class.

| Attribute | Element | Meaning | Controlled by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data-sefaria-note` | `<span>` | An empty placeholder where a footnote was. Its value is the note's `key` in `notes`. | `allowFootnotes` |
| `data-sefaria-end-footnote` | `<span>` | An end-of-text footnote marker. The value is the marker's text; the element is empty. | `allowFootnotes` and `allowInlineAnnotations` |
| `data-sefaria-commentary-marker` | `<span>` | A commentary marker. The value is the marker's text; the element is empty. | `allowInlineAnnotations` |
| `data-sefaria-commentator` | `<span>` | A commentary anchor. The value is the commentator's name. The element is empty. | `allowInlineAnnotations` |
| `data-sefaria-label` | `<span>` | The commentary anchor's label, copied from the source when present. | `allowInlineAnnotations` |
| `data-sefaria-order` | `<span>` | The commentary anchor's order, copied from the source when present. | `allowInlineAnnotations` |
| `data-sefaria-overlay` | `<span>` | An overlay anchor's name, such as a reading division. It always appears with `data-sefaria-value`. The element is empty. | `allowInlineAnnotations` |
| `data-sefaria-value` | `<span>` | The overlay anchor's value. | `allowInlineAnnotations` |
| `data-sefaria-ref` | `<span>` | A Sefaria reference. On a former reference link, it holds the link's reference and the link text is kept. On a commentary anchor, it holds the reference that `commentaryReferences` supplied for that commentator, order and label. | `allowRefLinks`; on commentary anchors, `allowInlineAnnotations` and `commentaryReferences` |
| `data-sefaria-ven` | `<span>` | The English version title from a reference link, when present. | `allowRefLinks` |
| `data-sefaria-vhe` | `<span>` | The Hebrew version title from a reference link, when present. | `allowRefLinks` |
| `data-sefaria-slug` | `<span>` | A named entity's topic slug. The entity's text is kept. | `allowNamedEntities` |
| `data-sefaria-mam` | `<span>` | A Miqra according to the Masorah marking. The value is one of the names in the table below. | none |

### Masorah markings

`data-sefaria-mam` takes one of these values, converted from Sefaria's class names:

| Sefaria class    | `data-sefaria-mam` value |
| ---------------- | ------------------------ |
| `mam-spi-pe`     | `petuchah`               |
| `mam-spi-samekh` | `setumah`                |
| `mam-spi-invnun` | `inverted-nun`           |
| `mam-kq`         | `ketiv-qere`             |
| `mam-kq-k`       | `ketiv`                  |
| `mam-kq-q`       | `qere`                   |
| `mam-kq-trivial` | `trivial-variant`        |

### Examples

```html
<!-- Input -->
He has told you<sup class="footnote-marker">1</sup
><i class="footnote">A note.</i>
<!-- Output -->
He has told you<span data-sefaria-note="0"></span>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
Text<sup class="endFootnote">*</sup>
<!-- Output -->
Text<span data-sefaria-end-footnote="*"></span>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
Text<sup class="itag">a</sup>
<!-- Output -->
Text<span data-sefaria-commentary-marker="a"></span>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
Text<i data-commentator="Rashi" data-order="1" data-label="a"></i>
<!-- Output -->
Text<span
  data-sefaria-commentator="Rashi"
  data-sefaria-label="a"
  data-sefaria-order="1"
></span>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
Text<i data-overlay="Weekday Torah Reading" data-value="Monday"></i>
<!-- Output -->
Text<span
  data-sefaria-overlay="Weekday Torah Reading"
  data-sefaria-value="Monday"
></span>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
See <a class="refLink" href="/Micah.6.8" data-ref="Micah 6:8">Micah 6:8</a>
<!-- Output -->
See <span data-sefaria-ref="Micah 6:8">Micah 6:8</span>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
See <a data-ref="Micah 6:8" data-ven="The Contemporary Torah">Micah 6:8</a>
<!-- Output -->
See
<span data-sefaria-ref="Micah 6:8" data-sefaria-ven="The Contemporary Torah"
  >Micah 6:8</span
>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
See
<a data-ref="Micah 6:8" data-vhe="Miqra according to the Masorah">Micah 6:8</a>
<!-- Output -->
See
<span
  data-sefaria-ref="Micah 6:8"
  data-sefaria-vhe="Miqra according to the Masorah"
  >Micah 6:8</span
>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
<a class="namedEntityLink" data-slug="micah" href="/topics/micah">Micah</a>
<!-- Output -->
<span data-sefaria-slug="micah">Micah</span>
```

```html
<!-- Input -->
<span class="mam-spi-pe">{פ}</span>
<!-- Output -->
<span data-sefaria-mam="petuchah">{פ}</span>
```
